selfHelp.title: Self-help practices
selfHelp.subtitle: Simple techniques to calm down and feel grounded
selfHelp.banner: These short exercises can help between sessions when anxiety, stress or restlessness creep in. Find a quiet spot, get comfortable, and take your time.
selfHelp.disclaimer: These practices are supportive tools and don't replace professional care. If you feel worse or are in crisis, reach out to your psychologist or emergency services.

box.readyHint: Sit tall, relax your shoulders, and press start when you're ready.
box.completeText: {{count}} cycles complete — notice how your body feels now.

478.readyHint: Get comfortable, relax your shoulders, and press start when you're ready.
478.completeText: {{count}} cycles complete — notice how calm your body feels now.

belly.readyHint: Lie back or sit comfortably, rest a hand on your belly, and press start.
belly.completeText: Notice how slow and easy your breath has become.

grounding.readyHint: Find a comfortable spot. We'll move through your five senses, one at a time — there's nothing to get right, just notice.
grounding.skipHint: Fill in as many as you like — or simply notice and move on.
grounding.completeText: Notice how your body and mind feel now — a little more settled, a little more here.

see.label: See
see.prompt: Name five things you can see.

touch.label: Touch
touch.prompt: Name four things you can feel or touch.

hear.label: Hear
hear.prompt: Name three things you can hear.

smell.label: Smell
smell.prompt: Name two things you can smell.

taste.label: Taste
taste.prompt: Name one thing you can taste.

bodyScan.readyHint: Lie down or sit comfortably, let your eyes close, and we'll move attention gently from your feet up to the crown.
bodyScan.completeText: Take a moment to feel your whole body at once, resting and supported.

feet.label: Feet
feet.prompt: Bring your attention to your feet. Notice any warmth, tingling or contact with the floor, and let them soften.

legs.label: Legs
legs.prompt: Move up through your calves and thighs. Let any heaviness sink down and release.

hips.label: Hips & pelvis
hips.prompt: Rest your attention on your hips and pelvis. Allow them to feel supported and let go.

belly.label: Belly & lower back
belly.prompt: Notice your belly rising and falling with each breath, and soften your lower back.

chest.label: Chest & upper back
chest.prompt: Bring awareness to your chest and upper back. Feel them open gently with each breath.

arms.label: Arms & hands
arms.prompt: Travel down your arms to your hands. Let the fingers uncurl and the arms grow heavy.

shoulders.label: Shoulders & neck
shoulders.prompt: Notice your shoulders and neck. With an out-breath, let them drop away from your ears.

head.label: Face & head
head.prompt: Soften your jaw, eyes and forehead, and rest your attention at the crown of your head.

pmr.readyHint: Sit or lie back somewhere you won't be disturbed. We'll tense each muscle group for a few seconds, then let it go — noticing the contrast between tension and ease.
pmr.completeText: Your whole body is looser now. Rest here for a few breaths and feel the difference between tension and ease.

feet.label: Feet & calves
feet.tense: Curl your toes and tighten your calves — hold the tension.
feet.release: Let your feet fall loose and feel the warmth spread through them.

legs.label: Thighs
legs.tense: Press your thighs together and tense the muscles firmly.
legs.release: Release and let your legs grow heavy and soft.

hips.label: Hips & glutes
hips.tense: Squeeze your buttocks together and tighten your hips.
hips.release: Let go completely and sink into the support beneath you.

stomach.label: Stomach
stomach.tense: Pull your stomach in and tighten your abdominal muscles.
stomach.release: Soften your belly and let your breath move freely again.

hands.label: Hands
hands.tense: Clench both fists tightly and feel the tension in your hands.
hands.release: Open your hands and let your fingers rest, soft and still.

arms.label: Arms
arms.tense: Bend your elbows and tense your arms, drawing them in close.
arms.release: Drop your arms and feel them grow loose and heavy.

shoulders.label: Shoulders & neck
shoulders.tense: Lift your shoulders up toward your ears and hold them there.
shoulders.release: Let your shoulders drop and your neck lengthen.

face.label: Face
face.tense: Scrunch your face — eyes, jaw and forehead — all at once.
face.release: Smooth out every muscle and let your face go calm.

safePlace.readyHint: Sit or lie back somewhere quiet and let your eyes close. We'll picture a place where you feel completely safe, and settle into it one sense at a time.
safePlace.completeText: This place is always yours. You can close your eyes and return here whenever you need to.

arrive.label: Arrive
arrive.prompt: Picture a place — real or imagined — where you feel completely safe. Let it take shape around you.

look.label: Look around
look.prompt: Look slowly around your place. Notice the colours, the light, the shapes near and far.

listen.label: Listen
listen.prompt: Tune into the sounds here — gentle, distant or close. Let them tell you that all is calm.

scent.label: Breathe it in
scent.prompt: Take a slow breath and notice the air — its freshness, its warmth, any scent it carries.

touch.label: Feel it
touch.prompt: Feel the temperature on your skin and the ground holding you up, steady and sure.

safe.label: Rest here
safe.prompt: Let the feeling of safety fill you. You belong here, and nothing can reach you. Simply rest.

box-breathing.title: Box breathing
box-breathing.short: Inhale, hold, exhale and hold for equal counts of four.
box-breathing.intro: Box breathing balances your nervous system by keeping every phase the same length. It's a favourite of athletes and first responders for staying calm under pressure.
steps: Sit upright with your shoulders relaxed and follow the circle.
Breathe in through your nose for four counts as the circle grows.
Hold your breath gently for four counts.
Breathe out through your mouth for four counts as the circle shrinks.
Hold again for four counts, then repeat for a few cycles.

breathing-478.title: 4-7-8 breathing
breathing-478.short: A longer exhale that helps you unwind and fall asleep.
breathing-478.intro: The 4-7-8 pattern lengthens your exhale, which signals your body to relax. It's especially helpful before sleep or when you feel wound up.
steps: Rest the tip of your tongue behind your upper front teeth.
Inhale quietly through your nose for four counts.
Hold your breath for seven counts.
Exhale fully through your mouth for eight counts.
Repeat for four cycles, building up slowly over time.

belly-breathing.title: Belly breathing
belly-breathing.short: Slow diaphragmatic breaths to ease tension in the body.
belly-breathing.intro: Belly (diaphragmatic) breathing draws air deep into your lungs so your belly rises instead of your chest. It lowers heart rate and quiets a racing mind.
steps: Place one hand on your chest and the other on your belly.
Breathe in slowly through your nose so only your belly rises.
Exhale gently through your mouth, a little longer than the inhale.
Keep your chest as still as possible throughout.
Continue at a comfortable pace for a few minutes.

grounding-54321.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
grounding-54321.short: Use your five senses to come back to the present moment.
grounding-54321.intro: When thoughts spiral or panic rises, this sensory exercise anchors you in the here and now by gently shifting attention to what's around you.
steps: Notice five things you can see around you.
Notice four things you can feel or touch.
Notice three things you can hear.
Notice two things you can smell.
Notice one thing you can taste, then take a slow breath.

body-scan.title: Body scan
body-scan.short: Move your attention through the body to release tension.
body-scan.intro: A body scan builds awareness of physical sensations and helps you notice and let go of tension you may be holding without realising it.
steps: Lie down or sit comfortably and close your eyes.
Bring your attention to your feet and notice any sensations.
Slowly move your focus upward — legs, hips, belly, chest, arms.
Soften each area as you reach it, without forcing anything.
Finish at the top of your head and rest for a few breaths.

progressive-muscle.title: Progressive muscle relaxation
progressive-muscle.short: Tense and release muscle groups to melt away stress.
progressive-muscle.intro: By deliberately tensing then releasing each muscle group, you teach your body the difference between tension and relaxation — and how to let go.
steps: Sit or lie down somewhere you won't be disturbed.
Tense your feet and calves for five seconds, then release.
Move upward — thighs, stomach, hands, arms, shoulders, face.
Tense each group on an inhale, release on a slow exhale.
Notice the warmth and heaviness left behind as you relax.

safe-place.title: Safe place visualisation
safe-place.short: Picture a calming place to feel safe and settled.
safe-place.intro: Imagining a place where you feel completely safe gives your mind a refuge it can return to whenever you feel overwhelmed.
steps: Close your eyes and take a few slow breaths.
Picture a place — real or imagined — where you feel calm and safe.
Notice the colours, sounds and smells of this place.
Feel the temperature and the ground supporting you.
Stay here as long as you like, knowing you can return anytime.
